children: Canadian net trade looks to have been a drag on GDP at the start of the third quarter, since the sharp narrowing of the goods-trade surplus in July was due to a fall in export volumes as well as lower energy and metal prices, Capital Economics' Ariane Curtis says. The roughly C$800 million surplus was considerably below consensus expectations for about C$3 billion. The result is that risks to Statistics Canada's preliminary estimate of unchanged GDP in July now lie slightly to the downside, Curtis says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)
